title: Figma marketing website, c. 2022
lede: Figma’s early-2020s marketing pages, named with Gumroad as a source of the style.
summary: Figma’s landing pages as described by Malewicz in March 2022.

evidence.note: Based on Malewicz’s March 2022 article, which analyzes Figma screenshots, and on NN/g. No Figma page from that period was inspected.

styles.note: Malewicz (2022) names Figma and Gumroad as the “two main innovators” of neubrutalism, and NN/g repeats Figma as an example.

context: [Michał Malewicz, “Neubrutalism is taking over the web” (Hype4 Academy, first published 28 March 2022)](https://hype4.academy/articles/design/neubrutalism-is-taking-over-web) analyzes Figma landing-page sections: cards “purposefully inconsistent”, shapes like “template shapes from PowerPoint”, hard figure-to-background contrast, and thick, slightly quirky fonts.

[NN/g, “Neobrutalism: Definition and Best Practices” (Hayat Sheikh, 11 April 2025)](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/neobrutalism/) names “Figma's brand refresh” as an example, linking to [Figma’s October 2019 brand post](https://www.figma.com/blog/bringing-new-life-to-figmas-brand/) by Tori Hinn. That post predates the name and does not use it.
interpretation: Figma appears in early accounts as an origin point, but the evidence describes contrast and deliberate roughness more than the outline-and-hard-shadow component grammar. Treat it as an influence until a capture confirms the traits.
next: Capture Wayback copies of figma.com pages from early 2022 (the Malewicz article is archived from 8 April 2022). Check for outlines, hard shadows, and flat brights before keeping this placement.

rights.statement: Figma website and brand material. Link and metadata only.
